first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in costa rica' because it's on the list and I want to know if the legal side is real or a headache. The intro names the Registro Civil and the documents, and the government sheets are linked, so I can check it myself. Went to the FAQ first. Cost answer is honest that the registry is free, but every other cost (La Gaceta notice, notary, translations, apostilles) is a fee with no number. The big catch for me is buried in the body: 4 to 6 months and we have to sign the request together in person. Does that mean two trips from Brisbane? The page tells me to ask. Downsides (crime level, rips, crocodiles, malaria) are all here with sources, which I respect. Nothing on what Wedded Wonderland costs or whether they take a cut.

journey.quote: Costa Rica is on your shortlist, and before you choose a coast or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Straight answer to the question I came with, followed by the actual document list. Good start.
Intro says flatly 'It will.' FAQ and the recognition section say 'in most cases'. The hedge is the honest one. Match them.

journey.quote: There is no charge for the registry service of celebrating a civil marriage before the Registro Civil.
journey.reaction: Good, a hard fact. Then the next sentence lists four costs with no figures.

journey.quote: You pay to publish the notice in La Gaceta, and a notary, official translations and apostilles each carry their own fees.
journey.reaction: How much? The La Gaceta notice and the Australian apostille are government fees, they're published somewhere. Notary fees I accept might not be. Give me the public ones with a date, or say plainly they're not published.

journey.quote: Because you sign the request together in person, ask the Unidad de Matrimonios how that timing works for applicants who live overseas before you set a date.
journey.reaction: This is the catch. 4 to 6 months, and we both have to turn up in person to sign the request? So two flights to San José, or not? That's thousands of dollars and leave, and the page shrugs and says 'ask'. If the source doesn't say, tell me straight that it isn't published, and tell me whether the notary route avoids it.

journey.quote: The central office receives requests Monday to Friday from 7:00 to 10:00 am, with 10 places a day, and regional offices nationwide receive them from 7:00 am to 2:00 pm.
journey.reaction: Real numbers. 10 places a day is exactly the kind of detail that tells me someone read the source.

journey.quote: A notary is the second choice.
journey.reaction: For an overseas couple wanting a resort ceremony, the notary looks like the actual route. But I get no timeline for it. Registro Civil gets 4 to 6 months; the notary gets nothing. Is it weeks? Does it need the same edict in La Gaceta?

journey.quote: Are you in good standing with the Dirección Nacional de Notariado, with an enabled user in the TSE's system?
journey.reaction: A question list that protects me from a dodgy notary. This is what I'd want a planner to tell me.

journey.quote: Many couples sign the civil marriage quietly, then hold the ceremony their guests fly in for wherever they choose.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' based on what? Unsupported on a page that sources almost everything else.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
journey.reaction: Didn't expect a wedding planner to lead with this. Sourced, honest, and it's what my mum will Google anyway. Trust up.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Read the full Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica before you book,.
journey.reaction: Stray comma before the full stop. Tiny, but sloppy on a page asking me to trust it with legal steps.

journey.section: The documents you gather at home
journey.quote: That one-month window shapes your timeline more than anything else on the list, so order this certificate last.

journey.section: When to marry in Costa Rica
journey.quote: Count back from your date: the Registro Civil's average of 4 to 6 months, a civil status certificate no more than a month old, and 25 working days of registration afterwards.
journey.reaction: Earlier the one-month rule was about when you present the certificate, which is at the start of a 4 to 6 month process, not the wedding date. Here it reads like the certificate must be a month old at the wedding. Which is it? I'd build my spreadsheet wrong from this line.

journey.quote: Choose a region for how guests will reach it.
journey.reaction: Section is called 'Choosing your region' and never names one apart from the malaria warning for Limón and Puntarenas. Fine on safety, thin on the actual choice. Then it's straight to a Concierge link.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, in the rainforest or at your resort
journey.quote: Strong currents and rip tides occur on the Caribbean and Pacific coasts, lifeguards and warning signs may be absent on public beaches, and crocodile attacks have been reported on the Pacific coast.
journey.reaction: Downsides stated with sources. That's how you earn trust with me.

journey.quote: Deposits and contracts: whose name is on the contract, in which language is it written, in which currency are payments made, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: Exactly the question I've been burned on before. A planner telling me to grill the resort on this is a good sign.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, holds the whole plan together, from venue and travel to vendors and payments.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is where I ask if you take a cut from the resort. Nothing says. Claim with no proof: no real Costa Rica wedding, no numbers.

journey.section: Plan your Costa Rica wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it is where the planning starts.

turn_offs_found.quote: Because you sign the request together in person, ask the Unidad de Matrimonios how that timing works for applicants who live overseas before you set a date.
turn_offs_found.why: The biggest practical catch for an overseas couple (possibly two trips) is raised and then handed back to me as homework, with no plain statement of what the source does or doesn't say.

turn_offs_found.quote: You pay to publish the notice in La Gaceta, and a notary, official translations and apostilles each carry their own fees.
turn_offs_found.why: Four costs, no figures and no links to where they're published. For someone building a budget spreadsheet, unquantified fees look like the catch.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples sign the civil marriage quietly, then hold the ceremony their guests fly in for wherever they choose.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported 'many couples' generalisation on a page that otherwise backs claims with sources.

turn_offs_found.quote: Read the full Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica before you book,.
turn_offs_found.why: Visible typo. Small, but it chips at credibility on a legal-steps page.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the document list, the one-month civil status rule and the 25 working days registration wait, for our planning spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread: the notary question list and the resort contract questions (whose name, which currency, when deposits go non-refundable)

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, and the promises are concrete: AUD quotes, fee agreed in writing. But how the fee is worked out and whether they take a cut from Costa Rican resorts aren't answered, and the guide leaves the two-trips question open. I'd email those questions before committing to a call.

top_3_changes: In-person signing: state plainly what the source says about presenting together to sign the Registro Civil request, and if it doesn't address overseas applicants, say it isn't published. Add whatever the source pack holds on the notary route's timing and whether it also needs the La Gaceta edict, so an overseas couple can see which route avoids an extra trip.

Fix the timeline line in 'When to marry': make clear the civil status certificate's one-month window runs to when you present it with the request, not to the wedding date, consistent with the documents section.

Fees and loose bits: give the La Gaceta and Australian legalisation fees with source and date (flagged for checking), or link the exact fee pages beside the sentence; change 'Many couples' to something that doesn't claim a number; match the intro's 'It will.' to the FAQ's 'In most cases, yes.'; fix the stray comma in 'before you book,.'

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for the catch and the numbers, flagged unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers and paperwork help listed as deferred unanswered questions, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Top changes require no new business facts; any fee figure, notary timing or overseas-applicant rule must come from a source

open_questions.question: Does the source pack say whether overseas applicants must attend in person to sign the Registro Civil request (fact_02, fact_11), and does it hold notary-route timing or the La Gaceta and DFAT legalisation fee amounts? If yes, the two-trips and fee objections close with sourced lines; if not, an explicit 'not published' line plus a direct link is the fallback.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'getting married in costa rica' while Costa Rica is on the shortlist and he is comparing planners; relevance is 4 because the legal content is what he wanted, and enquiry likelihood is 2 because the two-trips question and his fee and commission questions stay open.
Business details (fees, commissions, ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deferred by the brief; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Rendered link text was quoted without markdown link syntax, as a reader would see it.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, documents, both legal routes, the timeline and the Wedded Wonderland sections, with a skim of entry, climate, region and certificate sections.
